nodes.summary: For an instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, its graph is the graph of the edge list $E$ on $n$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$. Pairs with an endpoint at least $n$ contribute no edge.
nodes.title: Graph of a PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers such that $E$ has no repeated entries, every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \ne v$ and $(v, u) \notin E$, and the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ can be partitioned…
nodes.title: PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers admits a partition into triangles when the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ can be partitioned into sets of three vertices, any two of which are adjacent in the graph of $E$ on $n$ vertices.
nodes.title: Partition into triangles

nodes.summary: An instance of PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES is a pair consisting of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, and a list of pairs of natural numbers, the edges.
nodes.title: Instances of PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES

nodes.summary: The decision problem PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES.
nodes.title: PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers is well formed when $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \ne v$ and $(v, u) \notin E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
